headlines.title: Companies promised AI gains— here's how the payoff showed up in earnings
headlines.summary: Santander, Novartis and other companies say AI is beginning to boost revenue, cut costs or improve profitability as investors seek returns.
headlines.article_text: AI investments start to pay off in company earnings Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Companies including Santander, Novartis and Standard Chartered say artificial intelligence is beginning to contribute to revenue, costs or profitability. Santander said AI initiatives generated 194 million euros in business value in the first nine months of 2026. Meta said its AI investments were delivering substantial incremental advertising revenue, while Alphabet reported Google Cloud revenue more than doubled in the third quarter. In this article BSBR Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT The dollar steadied on Wednesday after the United States launched strikes against Iran, while investors awaited key U.S. inflation data. Skaman306 | Moment | Getty Images Some companies are beginning to report financial benefits from artificial intelligence investments, as interest in the technology shifts from hype to measurable returns in the latest quarter. Corporate AI investment has surged as companies look to boost efficiency and become more profitable, reaching $581.7 billion in 2025, up 130% from the previous year, according to the Stanford HAI 2026 AI Index report . As CEOs tout the tech's benefits and hyperscalers like Microsoft , Amazon , Google and Meta are expected to spend $700 billion combined this year on its infrastructure, investors are looking for measurable gains. Now, with third-quarter earnings season underway, some companies are beginning to put numbers around those benefits. Santander puts a number on AI gains Spanish banking giant Santander said Wednesday that it saw AI initiatives generate 194 million euros ($216 million) in business value in the first nine months of 2026 . Santander Chief Financial Officer José García Cantera told CNBC that AI is helping the bank reduce low-value tasks so employees can focus on higher-value work. "This affects both revenue and costs, so we are actually in the quarter where we can actually link directly to AI a positive contribution," Cantera said. "AI is being embedded in all the processes that we are conducting at the bank, so it's really difficult to just say how much comes from AI, but clearly AI is improving the quality of our services to clients." Novartis and Standard Chartered see AI in results Swiss pharmaceutical giant Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan told CNBC that AI was beginning to contribute to the company's bottom line. Novartis reported third-quarter core operating income of $6.04 billion, up 10% year-on-year at constant currencies. The company did not quantify how much of that was attributable to AI but Narasimhan told CNBC: "I think this is the first quarter I've really seen AI start to improve actually our P&L on a tangible basis." "We're working on R&D [research & development] to see if it can really increase R&D productivity," Narasimhan said on "Squawk Box Europe" on Tuesday. watch now VIDEO 2:21 02:21 Novartis CEO says AI has tangibly improved P&L for the first time Squawk Box Europe "We're already seeing some of the productivity you saw in the bottom-line performance of what we can do with AI from M&S [marketing & sales]." Meanwhile, Standard Chartered Chief Financial Officer Manus Costello told "Squawk Box Europe" on Wednesday that the company is seeing AI "appear everywhere across the business." The bank reported third-quarter operating income growth of 14% at constant currency, excluding notable items. "I think you can see it in the top line growth that we're delivering, and you can see it in that operating leverage that I talked about," Costello said, adding that AI is helping managers drive better relationships with customers and generate more income. watch now VIDEO 3:05 03:05 StanChart CFO: Biggest fear remains the macro situation Squawk Box Europe "We're also seeing that strong operating leverage that I talked about, where income is growing much faster than costs, and some of that is because we've been able to deploy AI tools to improve core processes and enable us to scale those up very efficiently," he added. Carlsberg says benefits are not yet at scale Carlsberg CEO Jacob Aarup-Andersen said on "Squawk Box Europe" this week that it's not seeing AI benefits at scale, but the technology has impacted internal processes, cost efficiency, commercial and pricing processes, marketing and its supply chain. The company's revenue grew 4.9% in the third quarter. Big Tech points to AI-driven growth Elsewhere, tech firms are also reporting gains. Meta said in its Oct. 21 earnings that its AI investments were delivering " substantial incremental advertising revenue ," while total revenue jumped 26% in the quarter ended Sept. 30. While Alphabet's Google Search revenue growth slowed amid concerns about AI competition, Google Cloud revenue more than doubled to nearly $31 billion in the third quarter, it reported on Wednesday. headlines.article_text: SpaceX loses bid to toss NAACP suit over data center pollution Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points SpaceX lost its bid to dismiss a lawsuit filed by the NAACP, which claims the company violated the Clean Air Act with its use of gas-fired combustion turbines to power its AI data centers. NAACP filed its complaint in April this year against xAI, which is now owned and operated by SpaceX, Elon Musk's aerospace and defense tech conglomerate. In this article SPCX Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT SpaceX is building a massive gas turbine power plant in Southaven, Mississippi to power its data centers in the area. SpaceX's AI division, SpaceXAI, lost its bid to dismiss an NAACP lawsuit, which is proceeding in federal court in Mississippi, according to a judge's opinion released late Friday. The lawsuit claims that the AI division of CEO Elon Musk's aerospace and defense tech conglomerate violated the Clean Air Act with its use of gas-fired combustion turbines to power its massive AI data centers in Greater Memphis. The Colossus data centers and a power plant that SpaceXAI is also building in Southaven, Mississippi, have faced community backlash for years. The Southern Environmental Law Center and Earthjustice filed the suit on behalf of the NAACP in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Mississippi in April 2026. The suit alleges that between August and December 2025, xAI and its subsidiary MZX Tech, installed and operated 27 gas turbines in Southaven, Mississippi, "without an air permit or regard for the health and safety of people living nearby." (SpaceXAI is owned and operated by SpaceX, which has rebranded it as SpaceXAI or SpaceXSI.) The turbines emit smog-forming pollutants and particulate matter that can increase health risks and cause an unpleasant odor, among other unwanted impacts, according to the suit. Lawyers for SpaceXAI argued in their motion to dismiss, filed in June, that the NAACP suit should be tossed because the company's use of the turbines, which it characterized as "mobile," was exempt from permitting requirements. They also argued that NAACP didn't have a right to sue under the federal Clean Air Act, and suits by such community groups were unconstitutional. The judge presiding over the case rejected those arguments, writing: "Because the plaintiffs have statutory standing under the Clean Air Act, because the combustion turbines are not 'mobile sources' under Mississippi's SIP, and because the citizen suit provision does not violate Article II of the Constitution or the private nondelegation doctrine, the plaintiffs' claims will proceed." The decision comes about two weeks after the same court rejected a Department of Justice's request to end the case against Musk's company.
